title: Degron-independent recruitment of KAT2A expands the target space of CRBN molecular glues.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and parsed two processed mass-spectrometry tables from PRIDE (a public proteomics repository): wp-esf_719 (139,679 rows x 20 columns, 10,268 protein groups, 9,517 gene symbols, 10 runs = 4 DMSO solvent controls + 3 compounds x 2 replicates) and wp-esf_520 (107,265 rows, 9,011 protein groups, 6 unlabelled runs), plus one immunoprecipitation table (14,079 rows, 8 runs). Listed every file in all three PRIDE projects (PXD072224: 30 raw .d.zip of 0.4-3.9 GB + 5 search-result CSVs; PXD072306: 24 raw + 3 CSVs; PXD072361: 8 raw of 5-7.8 GB + 1 CSV); no sample-annotation (SDRF) or metadata file exists in any of them. Read headers of the other four whole-proteome CSVs by ranged GET: only one carries compound names in its column names; the other four carry instrument run IDs only. I recomputed protein-level log2 fold changes myself from the one annotated file and reproduced the paper's headline: KAT2A falls -1.02, -3.29 and -2.08 for compounds WM-03-166, WM-03-190-HCl and WM-03-222 while GSPT1 (the off-target they engineered away) stays at about -0.1.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The data availability statement, read from the PubMed Central author-manuscript HTML (cryo-electron microscopy map EMD-75101, coordinates pdb_000010dw, three PRIDE accessions, 'no new code'). Supplementary Data S1 (4.6 MB Excel), Data S2/S3 (PDF syntheses) and Tables S1-S2 are listed but not retrievable: PubMed Central /bin/ returns a 1.8 kB HTML challenge instead of the file, Europe PMC answers 'Article with id PMC13423211 is not open access', and Science itself is paywalled. All structure-activity, dose-response and in vivo numbers therefore rest on the paper description only.
verified.note: Compound identities for 4 of the 5 whole-proteome experiments are only in the inaccessible Data S1.

a1_downloadable.note: PRIDE processed CSVs download without login (I opened three of them). But the curated supplement Data S1, which holds the compound-to-run key and the summary tables, is blocked at PubMed Central and paywalled at Science.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL. There is no degradation column anywhere. The deposited tables are peptide-precursor intensities per instrument run; the label (protein-level log2 fold change versus solvent control) must be built by summing precursors to proteins, normalising, and joining runs to treatment conditions. For 4 of the 5 whole-proteome files that run-to-condition key does not exist in any public file, so the label cannot be constructed at all for them.

a3_inputs_present.note: Protein inputs are usable: UniProt accessions and gene symbols are columns, so sequences and AlphaFold structures join directly. Compound inputs are not: the glues appear only as internal codes (WM-03-166, WM-03-190-HCl, WM-03-222) with no SMILES; structures are in a PDF of synthetic routes I could not retrieve.

a4_units_stated.note: DIA-NN precursor quantities are label-free intensities on a consistent arbitrary scale within a file; usable after median normalisation, which I did. Units are implicit rather than stated, and are not comparable across the five files.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL. The modelling unit is a compound, and only 3 compounds have decodable whole-proteome measurements (2 replicates each). Treating (compound, protein) pairs as rows gives about 28,000 rows but essentially one true positive per compound: KAT2A. Everything else below -2 log2 in my recomputation is keratin and single-peptide noise from 2 replicates.

a6_fits_laptop.note: The five processed CSVs total about 122 MB and parse in pandas in seconds; peak memory under 1 GB. Raw .d.zip files (30-50 GB total) are excluded by policy and not needed.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Cannot be fully checked because the paper's own tables are inaccessible, but the directional result matches: my recomputed KAT2A loss with GSPT1 unchanged reproduces the paper's central selectivity claim.

a8_label_provenance.note: Labels would come from real measurement (data-independent-acquisition mass spectrometry of treated cells), not from another model's output, and are not computable from protein sequence features. A8 is not the problem here.

existing_models.name: G-loop structural matchmaking from 'Mining the CRBN target space redefines rules for molecular glue-induced neosubstrate recognition' (Science, 2025)
existing_models.score_and_split: Not retrieved beyond search snippets: reported to match degron templates against Protein Data Bank and AlphaFold2 structures and to nominate 1,633 human proteins as cereblon-compatible, validated biochemically. No held-out split reported in what I saw.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Degron-independent (non-G-loop) recruitment, which is exactly what the present KAT2A paper demonstrates.

existing_models.name: Degpred, a deep-learning degron predictor ('Systematic prediction of degrons and E3 ubiquitin ligase binding via deep learning', PMC9281121)
existing_models.score_and_split: Not retrieved beyond search snippets; predicts general degrons from protein sequence proteome-wide, with a web server.

existing_models.name: MetaDegron, a protein-language-model predictor of E3-ligase-targeted degrons (Briefings in Bioinformatics, 2024)
Interpretable machine learning on proteomic plus chemical fingerprints ('Integrated proteomic screening reveals design principles of CRBN molecular glue degraders', bioRxiv 2026)
existing_models.score_and_split: Not retrieved beyond search snippets: 960-compound library, 230+ depleted proteins, 124 new cereblon neosubstrates, over half without a predicted G-loop degron.

existing_models.name: Monte Rosa Therapeutics QuEEN-style artificial-intelligence engine for cereblon-degradable proteome

backbone.name: ESM-2 (a protein language model) on protein sequence, optionally with AlphaFold-predicted surface features
backbone.hardware: Laptop CPU: about 9,500 proteins embedded with the 150M-parameter checkpoint in a few hours.

integration.partner_dataset: The 960-compound cereblon degrader proteomics screen (bioRxiv 2026) and the cereblon neosubstrate landscape (Nature Communications 2025), plus AlphaFold DB structures and UniProt
integration.join_key: UniProt accession / gene symbol, both present as columns in the PRIDE tables
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Which surface features make a human protein recruitable by cereblon when no classical degron is present - but answering it needs those large screens as the training set, with this paper's three compounds serving at most as a single held-out test case.

controls.positive_control: KAT2A must drop and GSPT1 must not, which I verified holds in the recomputed fold changes (-3.29 versus -0.14 for the best compound).
controls.negative_control: Shuffle run-to-condition assignments; the KAT2A signal must vanish.
controls.external_validation: The independent cereblon neosubstrate screens named above, joinable on UniProt accession.

honest_claim_h3: With this paper's accessible data alone, the only honest claim is that three closely related compounds deplete KAT2A and not GSPT1 in one cell line - a confirmation of the paper, not a model.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a protein's sequence and surface shape to predict whether a cereblon-based molecular glue drug will trigger its destruction.
plain_idea.train_on: Each example would be a human protein described by its sequence and predicted structure, paired with how much it dropped in abundance after cells were treated with a glue compound. In this paper only 3 compounds have usable proteome-wide measurements, each covering about 9,400 proteins.
plain_idea.predict: The log2 change in protein abundance after treatment, measured by data-independent-acquisition mass spectrometry of treated cells against solvent-treated controls. I computed this myself from the deposited peptide intensities.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Degrader chemists at Dana-Farber, Monte Rosa and similar groups currently find new targets by running expensive proteomics on every compound; a model that nominates recruitable proteins would redirect which proteins they try. Even a failure would map how far sequence alone can go.

more_or_better_data.why: Three compounds against the 960-compound screen in the 2026 bioRxiv paper and the 1,633 proteins nominated by the 2025 Science matchmaking work. This paper adds one new recruitable target, not a bigger dataset.

confidence_score.why: Two replicates per compound give a crude noise estimate within one experiment, but with one true positive there is nothing to calibrate a per-prediction confidence against.

models_beatable.why: The degron predictors (Degpred, MetaDegron) are sequence-motif-based and by construction miss degron-independent recruitment, which this paper proves exists - but beating them needs the large screens' data, not this paper's.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Fails the first condition: no existing model is runnable as a baseline on three compounds, and this paper's measurements are a single test case rather than training data.

ml_idea: Considered: predict degron-independent cereblon recruitability of human proteins from ESM-2 sequence embeddings plus AlphaFold surface features, using measured compound-induced protein depletion as the label. This paper's data cannot support it - 3 compounds, 1 degraded target - though it would be a good external test case for a model trained on the large public cereblon degrader proteomics screens.

effort.compute_note: Measured: the 122 MB of processed CSVs parse in seconds and my precursor-to-protein aggregation ran in under a minute on this laptop. The 20 hours is for reconstructing run-to-condition assignments for the four unannotated experiments, which I judge impossible rather than merely slow; embedding hours are an estimate from ESM-2 150M throughput on CPU, not timed.

verdict_reason: A2 and A5 both fail in the files. There is no degradation column: the deposited PRIDE tables are raw peptide-precursor intensities per instrument run, and the key saying which run got which compound exists for only 1 of the 5 whole-proteome experiments - for the other 4 it lives in a 4.6 MB supplementary Excel file that PubMed Central blocks and Science paywalls. Even using the one annotated experiment, which I processed and which correctly reproduces the paper's KAT2A-down/GSPT1-unchanged result, the modelling unit is 3 structurally near-identical compounds with one true degraded target between them, far below any usable sample size. This is an excellent medicinal-chemistry and structural-biology paper whose quantitative content is compound potency tables and a cryo-electron microscopy structure, neither of which is a machine-learning dataset. The project it suggests - predicting degron-independent cereblon recruitability - is real and worth doing, but its training data is the 960-compound screen in the 2026 bioRxiv paper and the published cereblon neosubstrate landscapes; this paper is at most one held-out test case.
